children: Oil prices reversed earlier losses Tuesday as traders weighed diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions against renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and persistent risks to regional oil supplies.
December Brent crude futures rose 0.6% to $116.54 a barrel, while December West Texas Intermediate futures gained 0.7% to $102.45 a barrel.

The rebound came as the Saudi-led coalition said Tuesday that it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia's eastern region, along with four drones targeting the kingdom's southern region, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey agreed to continue talks on regional peace and security after senior officials met in Tehran on Monday, according to a joint statement issued after the meeting.

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry said the visit was part of efforts to reduce tensions and support mediation by Qatar and Pakistan. The ministry called for opening channels of negotiation to prevent a return to military escalation in the region.
Meanwhile, Oman said discussions with Iran had produced an outline for a temporary arrangement to restore free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, although political obstacles remain.
Implementing such an arrangement would require compromises by both Washington and Tehran, Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said Monday in a speech at the University of Cambridge.
